document_title: Case File No. 002, One Line Rebuilt and One Left Alone

slides.headline: How do I pay a parking ticket?
slides.body: It lands on the same desk that answers 911.

slides.headline: The only number that always picks up
slides.body: At least four dispatchers a shift, around the clock, per Milwaukee Magazine. Roughly 105,000 routine calls a year, per the county. Cory Lynch, the operations supervisor, says being a 24/7 department made them the default for anything to do with municipalities or police departments.
labels: How do I pay a parking ticket.
Can I talk to an inmate.
source_labels: PER THE VENDOR'S OWN CASE STUDY

slides.headline: Then the accident call comes in
slides.body: "Then we have to put that caller on hold to answer a 911 call that could be for an accident, and then picking the caller back up and having them start their story over again if it happens to be another dispatcher that answers it."
labels: Lynch also says it has been really hard to hire and keep staff on.
source_labels: CORY LYNCH, OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR, TO WEAU

slides.headline: They rebuilt one line and left the other alone
slides.body: La Crosse bought it from a Seattle company called Aurelian. Every step above was drawn by a person before the phone ever rang. That is a workflow, rung 4 of five, and for this job rung 4 is the right answer. The vendor calls it an agent.
labels: ASK WHICH MUNICIPALITY ISSUED THE TICKET

slides.headline: A person typed the list
slides.body: If somebody in trouble calls the routine line, the system picks up certain hot words and sends them to a 911 dispatcher, per the county's operations supervisor. That list is not something the model worked out. Somebody sat down and typed it. The machine is matching words, not judging urgency.
source_labels: NO SOURCE WE FETCHED LISTS THE WORDS

slides.headline: 41,000 calls in seven months
slides.body: About 65 percent of the calls the system took never reached a dispatcher, per the county's own count. That counts calls that ended, not calls that got answered. No resolution or complaint figure exists on any page we fetched, including the vendor's own.
labels: 2024 BASELINE PER THE COUNTY · SHOWN ON ITS OWN SCALE
ABOUT 65 PERCENT NEVER REACHED A DISPATCHER
BASE · THE 41,000 CALLS THE SYSTEM TOOK
FOUR DISPATCHERS PER SHIFT, BEFORE AND AFTER
source_labels: COUNTY'S OWN COUNT, REPORTED BY NEWS 8000

slides.headline: The same product went sideways at another Wisconsin desk
slides.body: Ozaukee County bought the same product and went live around the clock in week one. Callers asked for a sheriff when they meant a deputy. Shouting and music confused it. They cut it back to two hours a day while the vendor worked through it, and the sheriff says the vendor has been receptive.
labels: SAME PRODUCT. SAME VENDOR. DIFFERENT BOUNDARY.

slides.headline: The bill goes up as it works harder
slides.body: About $67,000 in year one and about $81,000 in year two, per Milwaukee Magazine, priced on call volume. That is not a price rise. That is the product working harder, invoiced. Milwaukee Magazine put the annual price at about one employee with benefits. If your calls triple in July, model your July.
labels: PRICED ON CALL VOLUME, NOT PER SEAT
SEVERAL MONTHS OF TRAINING BEFORE THE FIRST CALL, 5 MAY 2025
OWNER · THE OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR, NOT IT
CADENCE · EVERY OTHER WEEK WITH THE VENDOR

slides.headline: Point it where a wrong route costs ten minutes
slides.body: Never point it where a wrong route costs a house or a hand. A caller here says a village name or a mile marker, which is a harder version of what broke Ozaukee. Test that before you sign. Under a few thousand routine calls a year, the honest answer is a better phone tree and an online payment page.
labels: MECHANICAL AND HEATING WITH A 24/7 SERVICE LINE
FORTY BELOW, NO HEAT. STAYS ON A PERSON.
WHERE IS MY TECH. WHAT DO I OWE. RESEND THE INVOICE.
WAUKESHA COUNTY RAN IT LIVE ABOUT 15 HOURS, THEN READ EVERY TRANSCRIPT
source_labels: OUR DRAFT, NOT LA CROSSE'S LIST

slides.headline: Milwaukee Magazine put the price at about one employee with benefits. La Crosse kept all four dispatchers.

post_copy:
A 24/7 dispatch desk with four people on it had become the default number for parking ticket questions and court times.

They bought a voice workflow, pointed it at the routine line, and left the 911 line alone. It took 41,000 calls in seven months, per the county's own count.
Milwaukee Magazine put the annual price at about one employee with benefits.

The deck has the five steps, both years of the bill, and the Anchorage lines this fits.

We do this kind of analysis for Alaska businesses, free. If you want your operation looked at this way, say the word.

What question does your after hours line get ten times a week that nobody is trained for?

#DispatchOps #AlaskaBusiness #AgenticWorkflows

Em dash banned. The base stays printed on the split rule, per the hard rule that the 65 percent never travels without its base.

slide_copy_corrections.why: WHAT IT TOOK must state the timeline in words, not only as a drawn bar, and in the one scoped form the fact-check allows. The bare label left the hard gate unstated in the copy record.
The numeral 40 traces to no claim and would flag in the numbers gate. Spelled out it reads the same and claims nothing.
Slide 9 carries 13 labels plus a body. Trimmed with every load-bearing element intact, the rung 1 escape hatch included.

slide_copy_corrections.was: They spent about the price of one hire and kept all four dispatchers.
slide_copy_corrections.now: Milwaukee Magazine put the price at about one employee with benefits. La Crosse kept all four dispatchers.

'The price of one hire' is Milwaukee Magazine's own prose (c12) and the hard rule says it carries that attribution in the same breath every single time. Unattributed it reads as the county's line, which would be a fabricated quote.

aftercare: Post it Tuesday to Thursday between 8 and 11am Alaska time. Drafts arrive daily, you own the cadence, so hold it a day rather than stacking it on another post.
Paste the FIRST COMMENT block within about 60 seconds of posting. The sources go there and nowhere else, and the close slide already promises them.
Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. A dead first hour is rarely recovered, and threaded author replies do most of the reach work.
At 48 hours note the saves, not the likes. If anyone asks what their version would cost, reply with the offer, do not pitch it in the thread.
